STL visits MIN tonight with the model expecting a tight one: 2.78 expected goals for MIN against 2.62 for STL. The teams create chances at an identical rate (3.27 xGF/60 each), so the gap is in prevention. STL allows 2.72 xGA/60, a bit better than MIN's 2.92, though MIN has the sturdier results (2.29 goals against per game, against 3.0 for STL). On special teams, MIN's power play generates 0.60 expected goals per game to STL's 0.43, and both penalty kills give up about the same (0.68 for MIN, 0.56 for STL). Both teams take four-plus penalties a night, so special teams will matter.

The goalie matchup leans MIN. Projected starter Jesper Wallstedt has saved 6.83 goals above expected in six games this season (.930), after 5.76 over 35 games last year. STL's projected starter Joel Hofer sits at 2.47 above expected in four games (.920), with a stronger track record behind him: 11.05 over 46 games last season. Both teams are on one day of rest.

Recent form is mixed. STL has won two straight, including a 7-2 win at OTT with a 0.66 expected-goals share, after a rough 1-6 loss at COL to open the stretch. MIN beat VGK 4-2 and FLA 4-1 while controlling the chances, but dropped a 5-2 game at WPG on Tuesday. The model likes Kirill Kaprizov most, with a 40% chance to score and 29% for two or more points. Matt Boldy (36% to score) and Quinn Hughes (27% for two-plus points) back him up. For STL, Mason McTavish leads at 25% to score.
